Das älteste Zinsbuch des Stiftes Hohenfürt.

Fol. II. Item census medius sancti Georgii pertinens ad pitanciam. Et circa festum sancti Michaelis eciam tantum. In curia Lochowycz 1 ix sol. In curia apum 2 ix sol. Nota in crastino purificacionis agitur anniuersarium de vna sexag. cum viginti pauperibus domine Johancze de Wellessyn 41 In crastino Benedicti agitur anniuersarium domini Dyethochonis cum viginti quinque pauperibus; datur prandium de vno talento. Item feria tercia proxima post pascha agitur anniuersarium Mykssykoni de Hodonicz, et conuentui datur prandium de quinquaginta gr.; de hiis dantur pauperibus ad portam lxx de. Item agitur anniuersarium Steynprechar in aduentu domini; datur prandium de vno talento. Item agitur anniuersarium Woytyechonis de Gywowycz; datur prandium de vno talento minus viii denar. [Item agitur anniuersarium Weczlini de Cypyn in die sancti Nicolai, siue in obitu suo, et datur prandium conuentui de vna sexagena gr. et xii de.] [De hiis dantur pauperibus xlii den.] [Item agitur anniuersarium domino Petro, sacerdoti de Rosis, et datur prandium ipso die de vii sol. et pauperibus xl gr. - et in die Etmundi (?) -] Fol. VII. Nota quod hec dantur pitancie abbate conuentui. In vigilia natiuitatis Christi dantur duo fercula piscium, et pistum, et albus panis pro halense vnus, et vinum. In "die sancto“ 42 dantur strawin, et chach cum vno ferculo piscium, et vinum. In circumcisione dantur owa in brodio. In epyphania domini preding, niues et chnechel 43, et vinum, et panem, si est in vigilia, vinum de gratia. Benedicti dantur ficus et pistum et vinum semel. In anuncciacione domini dantur esoces, vwa passa, amigdola et pistum et bis vinum. In die palmarum dantur esoces, ficus, pisces, pistum et vinum. In cena domini dantur esoces duplices, pisces, vwapassa, ficus, vinum et pistum. In vigilia pasche dantur esoces duplices, vwapassa, ficus, vinum,et pistum. In die pasche dantur due pitancie de ouis et vinum. In ascensione domini dantur duo fercula de ouis, et vnum de piscibus et vinum. In die penthen dantur duo fercula consweta et vnum de piscibus et vinum. Fol. VIII. In dedicacione ecclesie dantur duo fercula consweta de ouis et tria fercula de piscibus. In die corporis domini dantur due pitancie conswete de ouis et vinum. In vigilia assumpcionis beate Marie dantur duo fercula de piscibus et pistum et vinum. In die assumpcionis s. Marie dantur duo fercula consweta in pitanciis et vnum ferculum in piscibus et vinum. In natiuitate beate virginis dantur due pittancie conswete, vnum ferculum de piscibus et vinum. In die omnium sanctorum dantur due pitancie et vinum. [Anno domini M o CCCC o xix o in festo sancte trinitatis facta est conuencio census de incude Flaxlini (?) ad (sic) domino abbate Przibislao, ita quod idem Flaxlius debet dare ad festum Georii x gr. et in festo Galli totidem et non plus.] [Item in Chwaleticz Wenczeslaus et Jan habent de comunitate ibidem vnum hortum, de quo horto soluunt annuatim de censu xii de. et pro eodem orto tenentur comunitatem non inpedire in pellendo eorum peecora ultra ipsorum agros.] Anmerkungen. Vorstehendes Zinsbuch (liber censualis) ist durch sein Alter und seinen Inhalt eine gar nicht unbedeutende Quelle für die ältere Topographie des südlichen Böhmens. Sie ist namentlich nicht unbedeutend für Böhmen, wo derartige Quellen entweder noch nicht publicirt worden oder von dem Alter wie die vorliegende wahrscheinlich nur spärlich vorhanden sind. Nach Schrift und Inhalt ist dieses kleine Zinsbuch um das Jahr 1400 sehr sauber auf acht Pergamentblätter (in 8°, das erste Blatt ist unbeschrieben) geschrieben worden. Die Zeilen stehen zwischen sorgfältig gezogenen Linien und es ist häufig zwischen ihnen ein Raum leer gelassen, um vielleicht spätere Eintragungen leichter vornehmen zu können. Die nicht innerhalb Klammern stehende Schrift ist die älteste. Was ich aber mit Klammern eingeschlossen habe, ist im Laufe des 15. Jahrhunderts von verschiedenen Händen eingetragen worden. Die Sternchen bedeuten, dass an dieser Stelle eine ganze Zeile ausradirt worden ist. Dieses älteste Zinsbuch des Stiftes Hohenfurt enthält ausser der Angabe der Zinse auch ein Verzeiehniss der Jahrtage für die Gründer und Wohlthäter des Stiftes, das ich einmal schon wegen seines Alters und dann auch seiner Kürze wegen nicht weglassen mochte, und ein Verzeichniss der Pitanzien, d. h. der Speisen und des Weines, welche der Pitanzier (Küchen- und Kellermeister) an gewissen Tagen den Brüdern zu reichen hatte. Es hat letzteres Verzeichniss einigen culturhistorischen Werth, da sich aus ihm auf indirecte Weise abnehmen lässt, welch' einfache Lebensweise um 1400 bei den Brüdern Cisterciensern in Hohenfurt herrschte. Das nächst älteste Zinsbuch des Stiftes ist im Jahre 1550 angelegt worden. Es sei ferner hier bemerkt, dass, wenn es in den beigefügten Noten heisst: "Dieser Ort wird zuerst erwähnt“ etc., dieses "zuerst“ sich nur auf die Hohenfurter Urkunden bezieht.
entries.english:
The oldest rent book of Hohenfurt Abbey.

Folio II. Also: the half-yearly rent due at St. George’s, assigned to the pittance fund; and the same amount again around Michaelmas. At the farm of Lochowycz: 9 shillings. At the farm of the bees: 9 shillings. In both plots of Gerbert: 18 shillings, 20 deniers. At Boldau, and Boersyglag: 13 shillings, 14 deniers, and 1 obol. [And 60 deniers with oats once a year.] At Lyebenthol: 14 shillings less 6 deniers. At Przyezowycz, Merawycz, Bona Aqua, and Ralycz: 4 talents, 3 shillings, 3 deniers. There also, from the cottages, 28 deniers once a year. [And from a certain field, 20 deniers once a year.] At Restlens: 1 denier and 1 obol. At Ockol: 10 shillings. At the farm of Stokkern: [6] shillings. [At Kyrigslog: 1 talent and 6 deniers.] At Schestaw, near Hoerzycz: 3 shillings less 5 obols. [Also, from the mill near Stokharren: 13 groschen.] At Oppach, and Czedlycz: 21 shillings, 40 [9 deniers and 1 obol]. At Royken, Czwyenhlab, 19 (both villages), and Angrer, from one hide: 8 talents, 4 shillings, 11 deniers. From these, 9 shillings are given annually to the custodian for his office. At Scherleyns: 7 talents, 4 shillings, 12 deniers. At Pukkaus: 7 talents, 10 shillings, 21 deniers. From these, 10 shillings and 12 deniers are given annually to the community. [Also there, for the weekly table on the Assumption: 2 score and 5 groschen.] At Rosenberg, from the steward: 8 shillings. * At Nusdorff, annually: 10 shillings. At Horssaw: 3 shillings less 6 deniers. At Otyewyek: 4 score less 8 deniers, annually. From these, 2 talents are given to the community. * * [And from Wilhelm, steward of Rosenberg: 13 groschen. [At Haczlow: 13 groschen, and 8 groschen from (?) Safrano.] * [Also, at Kyssyelow: 6 shillings. From these, 60 deniers are given annually to the custodian for flour for the altar breads. [Also, at Waykerstarff: 1 “ius moncium,” 3 shillings and 1 denier, once a year.] [Also, at Kyrigsslag: 1 talent for candles for the early Mass on the Assumption, given to the custodian’s office once a year.]

Folio III. Also: the half-yearly rent due at St. George’s, assigned to the community; and the same amount again around Michaelmas. At Casclays and Wolech: 7 talents [and 31 deniers]. From these are given to the lord abbot 7 shillings less 10 deniers, to the custodian 4 shillings, and to the pittance officer 1 [shilling], 2 deniers and 1 obol. At Suchdol: [6 talents, 15 deniers, 1 obol, 40 groschen and 4 deniers]. From these are given to the custodian [5 shillings and 6 deniers, and to the pittance officer 7 shillings, 22 deniers, and 1 obol]. At Walchunow: [14 shillings, 52 deniers, and 1 obol]. At Otyewyek: 1 talent. At Rayntol: 10 shillings, 10 deniers. At Bukowsk: 5 shillings, 6 deniers. At Zahylays: 2 score and 26 deniers. At Chwaletycz: 2 score less 6 deniers. At Gebraslag: 7 talents less 30 deniers. At Marthatislag, from a certain field: 30 deniers. Also, from the mill at Slagel below Rosperg: 21 deniers. From all of these, once a year, 30 groschen are given for the meal of Lord Peter, formerly of Rosenberg. And on the same day, 40 groschen are given to the poor at the gate, and [1 score less 30 groschen] to the custodian for lighting, and 15 talents to the chamberlain for cowls. [And from the lamp of Stephen, the custodian receives less than 20 deniers . . .] (sic) [And from the lamp of the Holy Cross: 50 talents.] [And from the lamp before the chapel of the Blessed Virgin and for candles for the “Salve Regina”: 10 shillings, 12 deniers.] [And for the lamp before the chapel of the sick: ½ talent.] [And for the tithe sold at Passerslog, and Czypin: 3 score.] [Also, at Gastlass, and at a separate meadow, from which 16 deniers are given annually, half at St. George’s feast and half at St. Gall’s. Simon Chromar holds that meadow.] [The total annual rent belonging to the community amounts altogether to 66 talents, 7 shillings, 26 deniers.] [Of this, the person governing the community is required to pay 30 talents and 62 deniers to the offices assigned to him.]

Folio IV. [Total annual rent assigned to the pittance fund. The pittance officer is required to distribute some of it to the places assigned to him and to carry out the work of the pittance office with the remainder.] [Altogether it amounts to 112 talents less 6 deniers.]

Folio V. Note: On the day after the Purification, the anniversary of Lady Johancze of Wellessyn, is observed with 20 poor people, at a cost of 1 score. On the day after St. Benedict’s feast, the anniversary of Lord Dyethochonis is observed with 25 poor people; a meal costing 1 talent is given. Also, on the Tuesday after Easter, the anniversary of Mykssykoni of Hodonicz is observed, and the convent is given a meal costing 50 groschen; 70 deniers are given from this to the poor at the gate. Also, on the third day after St. Bartholomew’s, the anniversary of the lords Heinrich von Rosenberg and Hermann von Mylyczym is observed with 40 poor people; the convent is given a meal costing 1 score. Also, on the day after St. Peter ad Vincula, the anniversary of Nikolaus called Przyporzycze, burgrave of Wyldensteyn, is observed, and the convent is given a meal costing 1 talent. Also, on the third day after St. Nicholas’s, the anniversary of Lord Heinrich von Plumaw is observed with 40 poor people; a meal costing 1 score is given. The anniversary of Lady Offcze is also observed after Easter; a meal costing 1 talent is given. On St. Denis’s day the anniversary of Lord Gregory of Herslag is observed; a meal costing 9 shillings is given to the convent.

Folio VI. Also, the anniversary of Steynprechar is observed during Advent; a meal costing 1 talent is given. The anniversary of Woytyechon of Gywowycz is also observed; a meal costing 1 talent less 8 deniers is given. [The anniversary of Weczlin of Cypyn is observed on St. Nicholas’s day, or on the day of his death, and the convent is given a meal costing 1 score of groschen and 12 deniers.] [42 deniers are given from this to the poor.] [The anniversary of Lord Peter, priest of Rosis, is also observed, and that day a meal costing 7 shillings is given, and 40 groschen to the poor — and on the day of Etmundi (?)]

Folio VII. Note: The following are given by the abbot to the convent as pittance. On Christmas Eve, two fish dishes, baked food, white bread for one person from the Halen, and wine are given. On “the holy day,” strawin and chach with one fish dish and wine are given. On the feast of the Circumcision, eggs in broth are given. On Epiphany, preding, niues, and chnechel, and wine are given; bread too, if it falls on a vigil; wine is given as an extra. On St. Benedict’s day, figs, baked food, and wine are given once. On the Annunciation, esoces, raisins, almonds, baked food, and wine are given twice. On Palm Sunday, esoces, figs, fish, baked food, and wine are given. On Maundy Thursday, double portions of esoces, fish, raisins, figs, wine, and baked food are given. On Easter Eve, double portions of esoces, raisins, figs, wine, and baked food are given. On Easter Sunday, two egg dishes and wine are given. On Ascension Day, two egg dishes, one fish dish, and wine are given. On Pentecost, two customary dishes and one fish dish, and wine, are given.

Folio VIII. On the church’s dedication feast, two customary egg dishes and three fish dishes are given. On Corpus Christi, two customary egg pottages and wine are given. On the vigil of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, two fish dishes, baked food, and wine are given. On the Assumption of St. Mary, two customary pottages and one fish dish, and wine, are given. On the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin, two customary pottages, one fish dish, and wine are given. On All Saints’ Day, two pottages and wine are given. [In the year of the Lord 1419, on Trinity Sunday, a rent agreement was made for Flaxlini’s forge (?) by Abbot Przibislaus, so that Flaxlius must pay 10 groschen at St. George’s feast and the same at St. Gall’s feast, and no more.] [Also, at Chwaleticz, Wenczeslaus and Jan hold from the community a garden there, for which they pay annually 12 deniers in rent, and in return for the garden they must not hinder the community from driving its livestock beyond their fields.]

Notes. By its age and contents, the above rent book (liber censualis) is a source of considerable importance for the early topography of southern Bohemia. It is especially important for Bohemia, where sources of this kind either have not yet been published or, if as old as this one, are probably scarce. Judging by its writing and contents, this little rent book of the Hohenfurt Abbey was carefully written around the year 1400 on eight parchment leaves (in octavo; the first leaf is blank). The lines are between carefully ruled lines, and spaces are often left between them, perhaps to make later entries easier. The writing not enclosed in brackets is the oldest. What I have enclosed in brackets was entered during the fifteenth century by various hands. The asterisks mean that an entire line has been erased at that place. Besides rents, this oldest rent book of Hohenfurt Abbey contains a list of anniversaries for the abbey’s founders and benefactors, which I did not want to omit, both because of its age and its brevity, and a list of pittances—that is, food and wine that the pittance officer (the kitchen and cellar master) had to provide to the brothers on certain days. The latter list has some cultural-historical value, since it indirectly indicates how simple the Cistercian brothers’ way of life at Hohenfurt was around 1400. The next oldest rent book of the abbey was made in 1550. It should also be noted here that when the appended notes say “This place is first mentioned,” and so forth, “first” refers only to the Hohenfurt documents.
